title: Flaky — A Test Suite Weather Report
description: A seeded simulator of a 24-test end-to-end suite where each test has a hidden flake probability and cause: timing, network, animation, shared state, order dependence, or one real product race. Run it 1, 10 or 100 times to build a pass/fail heatmap, then flip retries, quarantine and shuffle to see how each one changes the forecast, and click any test to get a diagnosis and a code fix.
prompt: Make me 'Flaky: A Test Suite Weather Report'. Simulate a suite of about 24 fictional end-to-end tests, each with a hidden flake probability and cause (timing, network, animation, shared state, order dependence), plus one that's actually a real product bug. Buttons run the suite 1, 10 or 100 times and animate a runs-by-tests heatmap with a suite-verdict row on top. Show flake-rate stats and a weather-style forecast of the chance the suite goes green. Add a retry toggle that shows how retries hide flakiness (and what they cost in CI minutes), a quarantine toggle, and a shuffle toggle that exposes order-dependent tests. Clicking a test should open a diagnosis panel with the evidence, a typical error, the likely root cause and a concrete Playwright fix. Seed it via ?seed= so it's reproducible.

methodology: Determinism first: a mulberry32 PRNG seeded from ?seed= always consumes the same random numbers per run, whatever the toggles, so the same seed gives the same history and the spec can compare two page loads exactly.

Metamorphic oracles instead of hard-coded numbers: turning retries on must raise suite-green and leave first-try failures unchanged; turning quarantine on must quarantine exactly the flaky count and reach 100% green.
Model invariants: stable tests never fail; order-dependent tests fail only when shuffled after their polluting sibling, so with shuffle off they are 0%.
Content correctness: the diagnosis panel shows the right cause and fix for representative tests, including the 'real bug' case that must warn against quarantine.
Visual check at 1280px and 390px for heatmap row alignment against the DOM name and rate columns, with the reduced-motion path used in tests.
risks: Canvas rows drifting out of alignment with the DOM name list when the row-height token or the suite-row offset changes.
Toggles accidentally changing how much randomness is consumed, which would silently break seed reproducibility.
Quarantine membership being computed from a stale history after reset or a new seed.
qa.playwright: The heatmap is a canvas, so the spec never reads pixels. Every number the canvas encodes is also rendered as DOM text (per-test fail % and the stat tiles), and the tests assert on that through data-testid. ?seed= made the simulation reproducible, but the stronger technique was metamorphic assertions (retries raise green and leave first-try failures unchanged), which stay true if the model's probabilities are retuned. The reveal animation is requestAnimationFrame-driven, so emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' }) makes it render instantly rather than needing page.clock. Screenshot comparison was avoided on purpose: a 2,400-cell canvas with anti-aliasing is a poor oracle, and a screenshot diff wouldn't explain what went wrong.
coverage: Seed reproducibility across two page loads
Quarantine count equals flaky count, 100% green, real-bug warning
Diagnosis panel content; order-dependent test green with shuffle off

a11y: Test names are real toggle buttons (aria-pressed) whose accessible names include the observed failure rate and quarantine status, and all toggles are labelled checkboxes. The forecast, stats and diagnosis are aria-live regions, and the canvas has a summarising aria-label, so the heatmap's information never depends on color alone (failures also carry a cross glyph).
